items.q: What three filters does Nate extract from Dario?
items.a: Dario did **not** publish a checklist. Nate turns the interview examples into: **own-capital loop**, **software**, **automated sales+support without a terrible UX**. He drops capital so a normal starter is not underwriting a book.

items.q: Why isn't 'I can build software' enough?
items.a: If every deal needs custom onboarding and a salesperson, it is still a team business. Repeatable offer, agent-answerable support. File converter / ad reviewer pass. Calendarly-clone and unproven outreach writer lose the panel.

items.q: What is the customer actually paying for?
items.a: **Proof**, not a dashboard. Mystery-shopper golden set → score, fails, diagnosis, client-ready report. One patched example is not reliability: 88 stayed 88 after a billing fix (non-deterministic drift), then 94 with a leftover data-export fail.

items.q: What does the founder still own?
items.a: Money and data. Claude qualifies the trial form and answers docs. It does **not** send, charge, refund, or delete. Clay drafts stay **marked not sent**.

items.q: What is pain → person → promise for this product?
items.a: Agencies still test support bots by hand. Buyer = AI automation agency. Promise = 16+ high-risk scenarios + fail locations + a client-ready report. 'All agents' is too broad.

items.q: What number is the headline vs the next step?
items.a: **$499/mo × 168** = $1M ARR. First milestone is **five paying agencies** that connect a real agent, use the report, and pay.
